title: Wind an extension cord onto a hand-cranked reel
instruction: Wind the loose extension cord evenly onto the reel, then release it.
context: Guiding the cord across the drum while winding prevents a pileup that can jam when the cord is pulled out again.
setup: An open 280 by 200 by 320 mm steel-frame reel with a plastic drum is secured on the table, axle 320 mm forward of the robot bases, on the centerline. The axle is 160 mm above the table. The drum has a 96 mm hub, 164 mm flanges, and 112 mm of winding width. Its 25 mm diameter by 82.5 mm long revolving crank grip starts 88 mm above the axle on the right side. A 900 mm long, 8 mm diameter PVC-jacketed cord is attached at the top of the hub, 38 mm toward the side opposite the crank. Its 26 by 20 by 16 mm plug is unplugged. The reel is angled 25 degrees so that the loose cord leads forward and to the robot’s left, crossing the tabletop with the plug end hanging over the far edge.
scoring: After release, score 0.5 if at least 42 cm of contiguous cord has wound within the flanges in at least 0.85 turns. Score 1.0 if at least 84 cm has wound in at least 1.65 turns with a wound centerline that spans at least 16 mm along the axle. Otherwise score 0.
reset_notes: Unwind the cord, return the knob above the axle, and lay out the unplugged tail as shown.
fidelity: Plastic drum and steel frame geometry come from an adapted open-frame model. The PVC-jacketed cord is represented by self-colliding capsules linked by damped bending joints. The model estimates cord bending stiffness and bearing drag.
